correctness.rationale: All dimension and field quantifiers checked: [J_n,J_n] subset J_n^2, so ceil(n/2) maximal. Odd case is product of independent consecutive vector determinants. Even case is a one-3-step-path expansion with conditional uniform second-superdiagonal variables; an exact first-odd-failure/last-even-failure decomposition gives active probability a^m+m(1-a)a^(m-1), with m disjoint two-zero-vector exceptions q^-4 a^(m-1). Direct full matrix exhaustive tests for n=4, q=2,3 and independent low-diagonal exhaustive tests for n=3..7 pass. Asymptotic derived from a positive linear leading coefficient.

In particular, uniformly sampled nilpotent Jordan strata and small-dimension commutator fibers do not imply its first/second superdiagonal path law. value.rationale: For the natural family of nilpotent Lie algebras of all sizes, the highest associative nilpotency index of a random Lie bracket is an invariant relevant to random commutator support and Jordan long-block occurrence. The exact parity law exposes a nontrivial geometric path phenomenon: a single third-superdiagonal step produces linearly many competing placements in even dimension, while odd dimension has one determinant path. Both structural effect and precise all-field formula are not routine substitution from uniform-nilpotent or independent-product counts.
